subject: DPA: request for limited backup/deletion exception + subprocessor list
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@olivetech.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: OliveTech Legal <legal@olivetech.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA follow-up: retention and backups

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Legal reviewed the DPA draft and has two items they need clarity on before we can execute:

1) Data deletion window: our data retention policy requires customer-initiated deletion to be completed within 30 days. Your redline currently references deletion from "production systems" but does not include snapshots/backups. We need confirmation on whether Redwood will accept a 30-day deletion warranty and, if not, an explicit carve-out for immutable backups.

2) Subprocessors: please provide the most recent subprocessor list and confirm whether any new cloud transfer subprocessors in APAC are being added. We require notice and a right to object for high-risk subprocessors.

Attached are the redlines from OliveTech legal (high level). Can you route this to your privacy/compliance owner and get back to us early next week?

Appreciate it—
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Vendor Risk | OliveTech

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@olivetech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: retention and backups

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the clear notes and the redlines. Looping in Neha (privacy lead) and Lauren (account lead) so we can address both asks. Quick answers up-front: we can accept a 30-day customer deletion SLA for data in live systems; we need a narrowly scoped backup exception for immutable DR snapshots with a maximum retention of 12 months unless otherwise required by law. Neha will propose exact language for the carve-out and confirm our subprocessor disclosures.

I attached Redwood's current subprocessor registry (v2) and our proposed DPA text for the backup carve-out (see attached DPA patch). If OliveTech prefers, we can also add a short clause that commits Redwood to notify customers of any new high-risk subprocessor additions 30 days prior to onboarding.

We're prepared to send a DocuSign envelope once language is finalized.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@olivetech.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: retention and backups

Samantha —

Following up with proposed text to resolve the snapshot/backups concern. Proposed new paragraph (to be added to Section 4.2 - Deletion):

"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer acknowledges and agrees that (a) Redwood may retain Customer Data in immutable backup and disaster recovery copies ("Backups") solely to meet operational continuity and legal obligations; (b) Redwood will, upon Customer's written request, initiate deletion of Customer Data from live systems within thirty (30) days; and (c) Redwood will exclude Backups from the thirty (30) day deletion commitment but will take commercially reasonable steps to: (i) limit the retention period of Backups to no more than twelve (12) months except where longer retention is required by applicable law; and (ii) ensure that Backups are protected by encryption and access controls equivalent to production systems."

Additionally:
- We confirm no APAC subprocessors are being added at this time; our current registry (attached) lists cloud providers and monitoring vendors.
- We can agree to a 30-day notice for any new high-risk subprocessor and a right to object for genuinely high-risk categories (e.g., identity providers, billing processors).

If OliveTech is comfortable with that tradeoff, Mateo can consolidate final redlines and route for signature.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Pike <mpike@olivetech.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@olivetech.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: retention and backups

Neha —

Thanks for the proposed language. A couple of follow-ups from OliveTech legal:

1) Twelve months for backups is longer than we'd like — is there scope to shorten to 180 days with an exception for legal holds? If not, can you add a requirement to provide quarterly inventory of retained Backups that contain Customer Data so we can audit retention?

2) Please clarify whether the backups are stored in a way that would permit independent deletion on request (we recognise immutability for DR images, but we want process visibility).

If you can take a pass at 180 days + legal hold carve-out OR keep 12 months but add quarterly inventory and the notification of any backup retention beyond 180 days, we should be able to proceed.

Marcus Pike
Senior Counsel | OliveTech

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Pike <mpike@olivetech.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@olivetech.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up: retention and backups

Marcus —

We can accommodate a compromise. New proposed text:

"Redwood will limit retention of Backups to a default period of one hundred eighty (180) days; Redwood may retain Backups beyond 180 days only where required by applicable law or where necessary to satisfy an active legal hold. In any instance where Redwood retains Backups beyond 180 days, Redwood will provide Customer with a quarterly report identifying the Backups retained and a rationale for retention. Redwood will maintain reasonable administrative and technical safeguards around Backups as described in Section 5 (Security)."

On the question of deletion mechanics: the Backups are managed as encrypted object-store snapshots with immutable lifecycle policies; independent immediate deletion is not technically feasible for snapshots in many cloud providers. That said, we can provide inventory and attestations, and when retention windows expire or the legal hold is lifted, we will delete content as soon as the cloud provider's lifecycle allows. We will add an S3-compatible lifecycle reference in the operational appendix for transparency.

If OliveTech agrees to the 180-day + quarterly report approach, we'll incorporate this into the DPA redlines and route the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
